events.text:
🇮🇱 Israeli judges urge prosecutors to drop bribery charge against Netanyahu
The judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu's [corruption trial](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60505) summoned Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to court and told her directly that most charges are difficult to prove, the Jerusalem Post reports.
They stated that the chances of conviction were low in both Case 4000 (bribery) and Case 2000 (fraud), and suggested that an agreement could be reached in Case 1000, the gifts case. The judges cited the absence of objective evidence needed to establish key facts, and serious doubt over whether Netanyahu was aware at the time that his requests were receiving unusually favorable treatment.
The judges had already recommended twice that the prosecution drop the bribery charge, most recently in June, but prosecutors kept it in place.
Netanyahu has been under investigation in several criminal cases for 10 years.
🔴 The most serious bribery charges were filed in the so-called [Case 4000](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71440), concerning lobbying for the interests of the country's largest telecommunications group, Bezeq, in exchange for favorable coverage on Walla, a popular news website controlled by the company
🔴 Case 1000 concerns suspicions that Netanyahu received expensive gifts, including exclusive cigars and champagne, from Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan, with the investigation estimating their total value at nearly $300,000. Investigators believe that in exchange for the gifts, Netanyahu lobbied for Milchan's personal and business interests
🔴 Case 2000 relates to the prime minister's attempts to reach an agreement with the owner of one of the country's largest media groups, Yediot Ahronot, on favorable coverage of his activities in exchange for passing a law that would limit the reach of its competitor, the free daily Israel Hayom
If convicted, Netanyahu faces up to 10 years in prison for bribery and up to three years each for fraud and breach of trust. He denies all charges and has called the trial a politically motivated ["witch hunt"](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78247) and "10 years of hell."

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
✈️ Aviation regulator pinpoints router glitch that took down US airspace
Lab tests have recreated the failure behind this [month's nationwide ground stop](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77746) which cost nearly 20,000 flights, reports CNN, citing sources.
👉 Investigators reportedly claim a new router at a remote radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, had an overlooked setting that clashed with the decades-old routers the FAA is retiring and flooded the system with data, leaving gaps in radar and radio coverage.
Software patches should prevent a repeat, and the ongoing probe is about 90% sure no hostile actors were involved.
[The technical glitch](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78038) is only part of the problem. The investigation has raised questions about how the FAA oversees contractors maintaining critical infrastructure.
♦️ maintenance work that once required at least six FAA employees is now often handled by one coordinator - only four such coordinators reportedly cover the entire country
♦️ the administration's push to accelerate maintenance removed an additional layer of FAA review, including assessments of operational risks 
♦️ private company L3Harris is responsible for maintaining the telecommunications network, while the FAA primarily monitors service performance rather than directly supervising installations
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy face congressional hearings on the breakdown, with upgrades paused and Duffy asking for another $50 billion.
